text: I learned hunting from my father.
He taught me that patience kills more than strength.
I have spent most of my life tracking animal movement patterns.
Some animals follow routes older than human trails.
These routes often align with terrain features others ignore.
Satyapala and I disagree about how dangerous the forest is.
He focuses on avoiding risk.
I focus on understanding it.
Both approaches are sometimes correct.
After the Agnikanda, animal distribution changed significantly.
Some species disappeared from familiar zones for several seasons.
They later returned, but not in the same patterns.
I recorded these changes but did not fully interpret them.
Bhumaka once asked if forest productivity had changed over time.
I believe it has, but unevenly.
Certain areas yield more game than they logically should.
Other areas yield less despite similar conditions.
Revati says some injuries cluster in specific terrain zones.
I have observed similar clustering in animal death patterns.
Tarala once followed me into a deeper hunting zone without permission.
She did not panic, even when she should have.
Nagadatta is beginning to show similar instincts.
That concerns me.
The palace-monument complex is visible from several hunting routes.
I have noticed animals avoid facing it directly in some areas.
Not all animals, but enough to matter.
There are forest zones where sound behaves differently.
I cannot explain this clearly.
Experienced hunters avoid those zones without being told.
I do the same.
